title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Deleting Duplicate Characters
summary: Given a string of lowercase English letters, you can remove any letter that appears at least twice.
statement: Given a string of lowercase English letters, you can remove any letter that appears at least twice. The goal is to return the lexicographically smallest string possible after performing this operation any number of times.
constraints: s contains up to 100,000 lowercase letters.
An occurrence may be deleted only while its letter appears at least twice.
Return the lexicographically smallest reachable nonempty string.
hints: Each distinct letter must retain at least one occurrence; extra copies may be deleted.
Maintain the current result as a stack and pop a larger suffix character when another copy of it still remains.
After scanning, delete any still-redundant suffix because shortening a string after an equal prefix is lexicographically smaller.
The exchange removes the earliest avoidable larger character, and remaining counts guarantee every pop is legal.
editorial: The exchange removes the earliest avoidable larger character, and remaining counts guarantee every pop is legal.

tests.explanation: Deleting the first c gives aacb, which is smaller than every other reachable string.
No letter repeats, so z cannot change.
